vedic_reference.note: The name Akhilbhav is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘अखिल’ (akhil) and ‘भव’ (bhav), meaning ‘All-Pervading’ or ‘Universal Existence’. It is a name that symbolizes the concept of the universe being pervaded by existence and consciousness.

data.cultural_impact: Akhilbhav is a name that represents the Hindu belief in the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom as a means to attain enlightenment and spiritual growth. In Hindu society, the acquisition of knowledge and wisdom is highly revered, and those who possess them are considered to be of great value to their communities. In naming a child Akhilbhav, parents are essentially expressing their hope and aspiration that their child will grow up to be a person of great knowledge and wisdom, who can contribute positively to society.
data.spiritual_significance: Akhilbhav is also a name that carries a deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. As the name suggests, it represents the all-knowing, all-seeing nature of Lord Vishnu and his divine discus, Sudarshana Chakra. The name is a reminder that just as Lord Vishnu has complete knowledge and understanding of the universe, so too can we strive to gain a deeper understanding of ourselves and the world around us. The name Akhilbhav also symbolizes the idea of 'knowledge as power', emphasizing the importance of spiritual knowledge and wisdom in achieving inner peace and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Akhilbhav was a renowned Jain monk and scholar during the early medieval period (11th century CE). He was born in the ancient Indian port city of Bharuch in the western state of Gujarat. Akhilbhav is best known for his work ‘Shukla Prabandha’, a Jain text which includes detailed commentaries on various Jain scriptures.

Another important work of Akhilbhav is ‘Prabandha Chintamani’, a comprehensive encyclopedia of Jain literature, which was a major contribution to the Jain scholarly tradition. This work is considered a significant source of information for various aspects of Jain philosophy, history, and literature.
